part.text: I've confirmed the issue: the ASCII fast-path in `c.redirect` passes raw CR/LF straight into the `Location` header (Node throws on it; other runtimes risk injection), while `encodeURI` would correctly percent-encode them. Delegating the fix and tests to an implementer.

input.prompt:
Repository: Hono (working dir is the repo root). Task: fix a header-injection risk in `Context.redirect` in `src/context.ts` and add regression tests in `src/context.test.ts`.

CURRENT CODE (src/context.ts, redirect method around line 768-780):
```ts
  redirect = <T extends RedirectStatusCode = 302>(
    location: string | URL,
    status?: T
  ): Response & TypedResponse<undefined, T, 'redirect'> => {
    const locationString = String(location)
    this.header(
      'Location',
      // Multibytes should be encoded
      // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
      !/[^\x00-\xFF]/.test(locationString) ? locationString : encodeURI(locationString)
    )
    return this.newResponse(null, status ?? 302) as any
  }
```

BUG: When `locationString` is pure ASCII (no chars above \xFF), it is passed through unchanged, so raw CR (`\r`) / LF (`\n`) end up in the `Location` header. In Node this throws; in other runtimes it is a header-injection vector. `encodeURI` (used only in the non-ASCII branch) already converts CR/LF to `%0D`/`%0A`.

REQUIRED FIX:
- Percent-encode raw CR and LF in the `Location` value to `%0D` and `%0A` respectively, regardless of which branch is taken, so no raw `\r` or `\n` character can reach the header.
- Preserve ALL existing behavior for valid redirects: plain ASCII paths/URLs unchanged, `new URL(...)` unchanged, multibyte strings still `encodeURI`-encoded, and already percent-encoded inputs such as `https://example.com/%hello`, `https://example.com/%E3...`, `https://localhost/api?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com` must remain byte-for-byte unchanged (do NOT double-encode `%`).
- Keep the change surgical/minimal; do not modify unrelated behavior or files. If you touch the regex for CR/LF, include the appropriate `// eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex` so lint passes.

part.text:
Done. The redirect header-injection risk is fixed and covered by regression tests.

## Change

**`src/context.ts:772-783`** — `c.redirect()` now always percent-encodes raw CR/LF before writing the `Location` header:

```ts
const locationHeader =
  !/[^\x00-\xFF]/.test(locationString) ? locationString : encodeURI(locationString)
this.header(
  'Location',
  locationHeader.replace(/[\r\n]/g, (ch) => (ch === '\r' ? '%0D' : '%0A'))
)
```

Why it's correct:
- ASCII fast-path no longer lets `\r`/`\n` through; they become `%0D`/`%0A`.
- The `encodeURI` branch already encodes CR/LF, so the `.replace` is a no-op there (no double encoding).
- Literal percent-encoded input like `%0d%0a` contains no raw CR/LF characters, so it is left untouched.
- All valid redirect behavior (plain paths, `URL` objects, multibyte, existing `unchangedURLString` cases) is preserved.

## Tests

Added 5 regression tests at **`src/context.test.ts:132-159`**:
- Full CRLF injection attempt → `%0D%0A`, `Set-Cookie` header absent, status 302.
- Lone CR and lone LF individually.
- Multibyte + CRLF (encodeURI path).
- Percent-encoded CRLF input not double-encoded.

## Verification

```
pnpm exec vp test --run src/context.test.ts

```

All pre-existing redirect tests still pass. Changes are left unstaged/uncommitted per git safety (`M src/context.ts`, `M src/context.test.ts` only).
